name: Connecting neural networks and classical algorithms
gist: Modern approaches unify neural learning with classical optimization methods (mirror descent, proximal, Newton). How do you combine their strengths for speed and reliability?
explain: Machine learning researchers use two toolkits: neural networks, which are fast at learning patterns from data, and classical optimization algorithms (like mirror descent, proximal methods, Newton's method), which have strong mathematical guarantees about when they work. Neural networks work but nobody fully understands why, so you cannot predict when they will fail. Classical algorithms are slower but come with proofs about when they succeed, so you trust them. A modern question is: can you combine them to get both speed and understanding? Take the speed and adaptability of neural learning and the guaranteed convergence of classical methods?

The challenge is that these two worlds use different languages. Classical methods assume you have a smooth loss function and can compute exact gradients. Neural networks work even when gradients are noisy or approximate. Classical theory gives convergence rates—the algorithm reaches a good solution after a certain number of steps. Neural networks have no such guarantees but work in practice. Bridging them requires translating between these languages and finding abstractions that both can use.

Papers take several paths. Some implement classical algorithms using neural networks as building blocks: use a network to learn a descent direction, then step along it the way classical methods prescribe, so you get the neural network's speed and the classical algorithm's proof. Others add structure from classical optimization into neural architectures: design layers that implement mirror descent or proximal operations, so the network inherits the mathematical properties of classical algorithms and you understand how it works. Some papers analyze neural networks using tools from classical theory: prove that a particular network architecture converges at the same rate a classical algorithm would, assuming certain conditions hold. Others use classical preconditioning (scaling the problem so gradients are more uniform) to speed up neural training because uniform gradients converge faster. A few learn to optimize: train a neural network that takes a problem as input and outputs good hyperparameters (learning rate, momentum, etc.) for that problem, so you get speed from learning and adaptation. The theme is unification: seeing neural learning and classical optimization as two instances of a broader framework.

papers.title: A Geometry-Aware Efficient Algorithm for Compositional Entropic Risk Minimization
papers.contribution: Achieves O(1/sqrt(T)) convergence rate for convex problems with demonstrated effectiveness on extreme classification, AUC maximization, and robust optimization.

papers.title: DADA: Dual Averaging with Distance Adaptation
papers.contribution: Simultaneously work for diverse problem classes including Lipschitz, smooth, Hölder-smooth, quasi-self-concordant functions without parameter tuning.

papers.title: Design Linear Constrained Neural Layers with Implicit Convex Optimization
papers.contribution: Derives closed-form solutions using Euclidean distance for efficient constraint enforcement (GLCLayer), validated on linear programming and real-world problems like partial graph matching and portfolio allocation.

papers.title: Lightweight and Interpretable Transformer via Unrolling of Mixed Graph Algorithms for Traffic Forecast
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive traffic forecast performance as state-of-the-art schemes while drastically reducing parameter counts through the unrolled algorithm design.

papers.title: MoSSP: A Momentum-Based Single-Loop Stochastic Penalty Method for Nonconvex Constrained DC-regularized Optimization
papers.contribution: Provides provable complexity guarantees for finding stochastic ε-KKT points in constrained DC optimization.

papers.title: A Linearly Convergent Proximal Subgradient Algorithm for Sparse Portfolio Optimization with Transaction Cost
papers.contribution: Establish global convergence and R-linear convergence rate via Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property with KL exponent 1/2.

papers.title: A New Approach to Controlling Linear Dynamical Systems
papers.contribution: Achieves runtime scaling polylogarithmically with inverse stability margin, improving upon prior polynomial dependence while maintaining regret guarantees.

papers.title: A Penalty Approach For Differentiation Through Black-box Quadratic Programming Solvers
papers.contribution: dXPP achieves substantial speedups on large-scale problems while maintaining robustness, avoiding explicit KKT differentiation difficulties.

papers.title: CLASP: Online learning algorithms for Convex Losses And Squared Penalties
papers.contribution: For strongly convex problems, both algorithms provide first logarithmic guarantees on regret and cumulative squared penalty: O(log T).

papers.title: Complexity of Decentralized Optimization with Mixed Affine Constraints
papers.contribution: Establishes optimal convergence rates for smooth strongly-convex regime and provides near-optimal methods for remaining cases.

papers.title: Discounted Online Convex Optimization: Uniform Regret Across a Continuous Interval
papers.contribution: Adapts to unknown discount factor; aggregation via Discounted-Normal-Predictor combines decisions of experts with different discount factors.

papers.title: DisjunctiveNet: Neural Symbolic Learning via Differentiable Convexified Optimization Layers
papers.contribution: Achieves perfect rule satisfaction and strong predictive performance through end-to-end feasibility enforcement of hard input-dependent mixed-integer linear constraints.

papers.title: Efficient Spatially-Variant Convolution via Differentiable Sparse Kernel Complex
papers.contribution: Achieves higher fidelity than simulated annealing and lower cost than low-rank decompositions for mobile imaging and real-time rendering applications.

papers.title: Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader for Decoupled Bandits: Best-of-Both-Worlds and Practicality
papers.contribution: Achieves Best-of-Both-Worlds guarantee with constant regret in stochastic regime and optimal O(sqrt(KT)) regret in adversarial regime while improving runtime.

papers.title: Hinge Regression Tree: A Newton Method for Oblique Regression Tree Splitting
papers.contribution: Achieves fast, stable convergence with universal approximator status and O(δ²) approximation rate, matching or outperforming baselines with more compact structures.

papers.title: Lightweight Transformer for EEG Classification via Balanced Signed Graph Algorithm Unrolling
papers.contribution: Achieved classification performance comparable to deep learning with dramatically fewer parameters through algorithm unrolling.

papers.title: Logarithmic Switching Regret for Online Convex Optimization
papers.contribution: Achieves logarithmic switching regret bounds for exponentially concave and strongly convex functions, extending prior results beyond general convex settings.

papers.title: Noisy Pairwise-Comparison Random Search for Smooth Nonconvex Optimization
papers.contribution: NCRS achieves ε-first-order stationarity with comparison complexity O(k/(p²ε²)) for uniform-margin oracles and O(k²/ε⁴) for gap-dependent oracles, providing intrinsic-dimension convergence guarantees.

papers.title: Online Inventory Optimization in Non-Stationary Environment
papers.contribution: The method achieves near-optimal dynamic regret guarantee for non-stationary environments and improves static regret by a factor of sqrt(L_max).

papers.title: Operator Splitting with Hamilton-Jacobi-based Proximals
papers.contribution: Preserves convergence guarantees when replacing exact proximal steps with HJ-Prox under mild assumptions and demonstrates competitive effectiveness on statistical learning tasks.

papers.title: Optimal Anytime Algorithms for Online Convex Optimization with Adversarial Constraints
papers.contribution: Achieves O(√t) regret and Õ(√t) cumulative constraint violation for all t≥1, with adaptive bounds for dynamic regret and optimistic settings.

papers.title: QPKO: Differentiable QP-Embedded Deep Koopman Framework for Modeling Nonlinear Systems
papers.contribution: Achieves improvements in modeling accuracy, training efficiency, and control performance on four nonlinear dynamical systems.

papers.title: Trainable Nonexpansive Denoisers for Contractive Image Reconstruction
papers.contribution: Develop provably contractive reconstruction mechanism with global convergence while maintaining competitive denoising performance.
